key_insight: The paper turns neutral-atom hardware constraints into algebraic decomposition and graph-coloring problems to compile quantum gates with much lower addressing and transport overhead.
engineering_relevance: This enables more scalable compilation for two-dimensional neutral-atom quantum processors, directly reducing a major hardware bottleneck in practical circuit execution.
method: Use algebraic structure of single-qubit gate families to derive efficient rank-one decompositions and minimize addressing layers.
Model C-Z transport scheduling with graph-theoretic formulations to optimize atom movement under realistic constraints.
Apply the framework to structured circuits such as QAOA for MaxCut to cut transport cost at compile time.
evidence_signal: Experiments in the abstract report up to 2× fewer addressing layers for single-qubit families, about 50% fewer atom transport operations for C-Z gates, and over 30% average transport-cost reduction on QAOA MaxCut circuits.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on exploiting structure in the target gate families and on how closely the hardware and transport model match real neutral-atom device behavior.
paper_title: Structure-Aware Compilation for Scalable Neutral-Atom Quantum Computing
